avoid_supplements.name: Digestive enzyme supplements (amylase, maltase)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Directly counteract acarbose's mechanism by breaking down disaccharides and oligosaccharides, reducing drug efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; separate timing by at least 2 hours if necessary

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose chromium picolinate
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate hypoglycemic effects leading to additive glucose-lowering activity
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor blood glucose closely; coordinate with prescriber before use

caution_supplements.name: Fenugreek seeds
caution_supplements.mechanism: Additional mild glucose-lowering effect may occur with combination therapy
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for hypoglycemia; coordinate dosing with healthcare provider

caution_supplements.name: Alpha-lipoic acid
caution_supplements.mechanism: May enhance insulin sensitivity and glucose utilization
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood glucose; adjust acarbose dose if hypoglycemia develops

avoid_foods.name: Simple sugars and refined carbohydrates (candy, pastries, sugary beverages)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Acarbose delays carbohydrate absorption; simple sugars bypass this mechanism causing hyperglycemia and gastrointestinal distress
avoid_foods.action: Strictly limit intake; educate patient on complex carbohydrate preference

avoid_foods.name: High-fat, high-sugar foods (desserts, fried foods)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Increases gastrointestinal side effects (flatulence, diarrhea) and may impair glycemic control
avoid_foods.action: Counsel on low-fat, high-fiber diet alignment with acarbose therapy

caution_foods.name: Lactose-containing products (milk, ice cream)
caution_foods.mechanism: Acarbose delays lactose digestion; may increase GI side effects in sensitive individuals
caution_foods.action: Start with small portions; monitor GI tolerance and consider lactose-free alternatives

caution_foods.name: High-fiber foods (beans, whole grains)
caution_foods.mechanism: Combined effect may exacerbate gas, bloating, and diarrhea, though beneficial for glycemic control
caution_foods.action: Introduce gradually and maintain adequate hydration; benefits often outweigh side effects

monitoring_notes: Monitor HbA1c and fasting glucose regularly to assess efficacy and detect hypoglycemia. Educate patients that acarbose works best with a structured meal plan emphasizing complex carbohydrates, adequate fiber, and consistent meal timing; GI side effects typically diminish over 4-8 weeks.
